_comment: Checks known to fail, and why. CI reports them but does not fail on them. A check NOT listed here that fails is a regression and fails the build. Remove an id from this list the moment it is fixed.
_seeded: Seeded 2026-09-21 from the first real run with the eight leaks the review documented at v6.7.0. Phase 1 of docs/STEALTH_REVIEW_2026-09.md closed seven of them on 2026-09-21 and they were deleted from this list in the same commit: navigator-webdriver, useragentdata-brands, headless-markers, worker-platform, worker-hardware-concurrency, worker-languages, ua-version-vs-binary. Re-measured after the fixes on macOS arm64 (Chromium 151.0.7922.34 + Camoufox 135.0.1-beta.24, Playwright 1.62.1, residential AS7922): 19 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip — the skip is useragentdata-brands on camoufox, which Firefox does not expose.

_findings.persona-os-vs-host: camoufox only, and PLATFORM-DEPENDENT since Phase 2 — it now passes on macOS and Windows hosts and still fails on Linux. Chromium passes deterministically since Phase 1. The original cause was upstream's: camoufox npm 0.1.19 accepts the documented `os` option, validates it, then drops it (it forwards `{ screen, os }` to fingerprint-generator, whose option is `operatingSystems: string[]`), so the OS was drawn from market share — a Mac persona about one launch in three on a Mac host. Phase 2 generates the persona itself in CamoufoxAdapter._pinnedFingerprint() and can therefore use the correct key, which closed it on macOS (measured 19 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip). It CANNOT be closed on Linux with the pinned 135 binary: browserforge has no Firefox 135 + Linux persona at all and throws 'No headers based on this input can be generated', so the adapter falls back to a version-only pin and the persona claims Windows on a Linux host. That is the honest state — a coherent version on an incoherent OS. It stays listed because CI and the hosted instance both run Linux. Removing it requires either a Camoufox build on a Firefox version browserforge knows for Linux, or the maintained camoufox-js client.
